chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who goes to a money-changer with dirhams, seeking better quality ones, so they agree on his dirhams, adding a specific amount for something they have mutually agreed upon. Then he gives him dinars in exchange for those dirhams. Then he sells those dinars for those same dirhams based on what they had agreed upon initially. He (the Imam) said: 'Is that not with the mutual consent of both of them?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'There is no harm in it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to exchange coins for better quality ones by adding extra money in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a multi-step currency exchange where a buyer pays extra for superior quality, confirming that mutual consent (taradhin) renders the transaction permissible despite the addition of value. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between riba al-fadl (excess in exchange of same commodities) and riba al-nasi'ah (delay), emphasizing that when the added value is for a distinct quality difference rather than mere delay, it is not considered usury. The hadith underscores the principle that commercial flexibility is permitted provided both parties are fully aware and agree to the specific terms of the exchange.
